messages:
alex_support: FYI — acme-prod (acct acme-123) reporting KMS key access failures after private deployment maintenance. Redwood API returns 504 / "dial tcp: i/o timeout" and occasional TLS handshake failures. Can someone take a look? root traces attached.

customer_acme_ops: saw first spike at 2026-03-15T09:14Z. We didn't change ACLs except the egress allowlist for internal kms hostnames. Putting sample curl below.

customer_acme_ops:
```
curl -v https://kms-us-1.internal.acme-kms:443/v1/keys/abc -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." --max-time 10
*   Trying 10.10.5.22:443...
* connect to 10.10.5.22 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Operation timed out after 10001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
curl: (28) Operation timed out
```

jordan_eng: can you run dig +trace and openssl s_client with -servername and paste outputs? Also tcpdump while reproducing would help.

customer_acme_ops:
```
$ dig kms-us-1.internal.acme-kms @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 48722
;; flags: qr; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;kms-us-1.internal.acme-kms. IN A
```

customer_acme_ops: dig sometimes returns an A record (10.10.5.22) with TTL 5, then SERVFAIL for a minute. dns TTL churn.

maria_sre: possible DNS forwarding loop or intermittent DNSSEC failure from their resolver. Also check NAT gateway health — ephemeral port exhaustion will cause connect() timeouts.

jordan_eng: try openssl to check SNI/cert:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.22:443 -servername kms-us-1.internal.acme-kms
CONNECTED(00000003)
140506....+err:error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
---
subject=CN = kms-prod.redwood-kms.com
---
```

jordan_eng: this shows TLS alert unknown ca and cert CN is kms-prod.redwood-kms.com while client expects kms-us-1.internal.acme-kms — looks like a TLS interception or proxy rewriting certs, or the HSM cluster serving a public cert CN we don't expect. Any TLS-inspecting firewall in path?

customer_acme_ops: we do have a perimeter TLS-inspection appliance for outbound traffic. It does MITM with a corporate CA. But we previously had a rule to bypass redwood-* hostnames, not sure internal names are included. We added the internal name to bypass and restarted the appliance, will test.

customer_acme_ops:
```
After bypass: curl returns 200 but still ~2% of calls see TLS handshake errors and some calls time out. tcpdump shows SYN retransmits and then RST from 10.10.5.22 after 3rd retransmit.
12:14:35.123456 IP 172.20.5.10.50124 > 10.10.5.22.443: S
12:14:35.123999 IP 172.20.5.10.50124 > 10.10.5.22.443: S (retransmit)
12:14:35.125111 IP 10.10.5.22.443 > 172.20.5.10.50124: R
```

maria_sre: RST from server could be HSM side rejecting connection: check server-side conn limit or health. Also confirm client's source ports not being SNATed unpredictably; if multiple flows share SNAT IP and HSM enforces per-connection validation it can cause resets.

alex_support: quick workaround — route KMS traffic through Hosted KMS fallback for reads while we debug. Jordan can you open an eng-runtime ticket to validate HSM cluster cert rotation and connection limits? I'll add SRE to loop.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation/kms-prod completed 2026-03-15T08:50Z (rollout 1/3), no failures reported in control plane.

jordan_eng: filed ENG-3241 with logs and packet captures. Assigning to eng-runtime (maria_sre) for cert + connection limit checks. ETA 2 business days. Action items: customer to keep TLS bypass in place, SRE to confirm NAT gateway ephemeral port counters, eng-runtime to verify HSM cluster TLS config and whether certs are replaced with CNs not matching internal hostnames.

maria_sre: I'll also ask infra to dump NAT gateway metrics and connection tracking. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
